marble.name: Photosynthesis
marble.subject: Science
marble.description: Explain photosynthesis as the process by which plants use light energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen, and describe how mineral nutrients are absorbed through roots
marble.prompt: If you was asked why plants don't need to eat food like animals do, could they explain how plants make their own food using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide — and write the equation?

cluster.summary: Your child is learning about the amazing diversity of life — identifying different animals and plants, understanding how body parts help animals survive, and discovering what all living things need to stay alive.

misconceptions: Believing plants get their food from the soil, or that soil minerals ARE the plant's food — minerals are needed in tiny amounts for making proteins/chlorophyll; the bulk food (glucose) is built from CO₂ and water.
Thinking plants photosynthesise instead of respiring, or that they only respire at night — plants respire continuously; photosynthesis is additional and light-dependent.
Assuming chlorophyll is a reactant that gets used up, rather than a catalyst-like pigment that captures light and is not consumed.
Confusing which gas is taken in and which is given out (mixing up the CO₂-in / O₂-out of photosynthesis with the reverse in respiration).
Thinking glucose is stored and used as glucose only — not realising it is converted to starch for storage and used to build the plant's biomass (cellulose, proteins).
representations: The word equation laid out as a process (carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen, with light and chlorophyll over the arrow) rather than a static line
A cross-section leaf diagram showing stomata (gas in/out), chloroplasts, and veins bringing water — the 'factory' model of the leaf
A whole-plant sourcing diagram: air (CO₂) to leaves, soil (water + minerals) to roots, sunlight to the canopy
An input–output 'balance' visual pairing photosynthesis with respiration (the reverse arrows) to show the gas exchange coupling
A rate response: brighter light / more CO₂ → faster bubbling, previewing limiting factors without quantifying them
authoredAnswer: Almost all the extra mass comes from carbon dioxide taken from the AIR, combined with water, using light energy captured by chlorophyll to make glucose (carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen); the soil supplies water and small amounts of mineral nutrients, not the bulk of the mass.
probe: Present van Helmont's experiment: a small willow planted in a weighed pot of soil, watered for years, grows into a large tree while the soil loses only a few grams. Before revealing the result, ask the child to predict how much soil mass will be lost and WHY. The predicted reason is diagnostic: a child expecting the so

wrongAnswers.wrong: It comes from the nutrients and food in the soil that the roots suck up
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: reason names soil as the source of the tree's mass
wrongAnswers.fix: use van Helmont's result — the soil mass barely changed — to show the mass cannot come from soil; establish carbon comes from CO2 in the air

wrongAnswers.wrong: It comes mostly from all the water the tree drinks up through its roots
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: names water or the roots as the food source, omitting CO2 and light
wrongAnswers.fix: distinguish what roots supply (water and minerals) from where the carbon and energy come from (air and light)

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: surfaces on the probe — says plants only photosynthesise and never respire, or calls photosynthesis 'plant breathing'
wrongAnswers.fix: establish plants BOTH photosynthesise and respire; photosynthesis makes glucose, respiration releases its energy

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: lists light alongside CO2 and water as a material built into the sugar
wrongAnswers.fix: clarify light is the ENERGY source captured by chlorophyll, not a material ingredient of glucose
